questions.e: Erythroplakia, a red velvety patch, often already shows severe dysplasia or carcinoma on biopsy and has the highest malignant potential of the oral potentially malignant disorders. Homogeneous leukoplakia carries a lower risk than red or speckled lesions.

questions.s: Rukhsana, 52, has chewed paan with tobacco for 30 years. At a dental check in Hyderabad, a 2 cm white patch is seen on the lateral border of her tongue. It is painless, cannot be scraped off and has not resolved 3 weeks after she stopped chewing. What is the most appropriate next step?
o: Topical antifungal and review in 2 weeks
questions.e: A persistent white patch that cannot be wiped off in a tobacco and paan user is leukoplakia, a potentially malignant disorder, and only a biopsy shows whether there is dysplasia or early carcinoma. Candidal plaques scrape off, so antifungal treatment alone would delay the diagnosis. Reassurance is unsafe because the lateral tongue is a high-risk site.

questions.s: A 55-year-old woman has a squamous cell carcinoma at the tip of her tongue. To which lymph nodes does this part of the tongue drain first?
questions.e: The tip of the tongue drains to the submental nodes (often bilaterally), the lateral parts drain to the submandibular nodes, and the posterior third drains to the deep cervical nodes. All eventually reach the deep cervical chain, including the jugulo-omohyoid node.

questions.s: A 20-year-old woman has a painless, soft, bluish, translucent swelling in the floor of her mouth to one side of the tongue, present for 2 months. It occasionally decreases in size and then recurs. From which gland does this lesion most commonly arise?
questions.e: A ranula is a mucus extravasation cyst usually arising from the sublingual gland, appearing as a bluish translucent swelling in the floor of the mouth. Treatment that removes the sublingual gland has the lowest recurrence; lip mucoceles arise from minor glands.

questions.s: A 62-year-old man has a painless ulcer on the lateral border of his tongue for 5 weeks. A dentist smoothed an adjacent sharp tooth 3 weeks ago, but the ulcer has not healed. It has a firm base. What is the most appropriate next step?
questions.e: An oral ulcer that persists more than 3 weeks after removal of a likely cause, especially with induration, must be biopsied to exclude squamous cell carcinoma. Further trials of topical treatment delay diagnosis.

questions.s: A 30-year-old man has a slowly enlarging, painless, bony-hard swelling at the angle of his left mandible over 2 years. Teeth in the area are loose but sensation over the lip is normal. An orthopantomogram shows a multilocular, soap-bubble radiolucency with expansion of the cortex. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: A slowly growing, expansile multilocular radiolucency at the angle of the mandible in a young adult is typical of ameloblastoma, a locally aggressive odontogenic tumour treated by resection with margins. A dentigerous cyst is unilocular and surrounds the crown of an unerupted tooth.

questions.s: A 65-year-old man has an advanced carcinoma of the floor of the mouth that has invaded the right hypoglossal nerve. When asked to protrude his tongue, what is expected?
o: Deviation away from the right side
questions.e: Each genioglossus pushes the tongue forward and towards the opposite side, so when one side is paralysed the healthy side pushes the tongue towards the weak side. A lower motor neurone lesion also causes wasting and fasciculation on the affected side.

questions.s: A nurse in a neurosurgical ICU asks the normal resting intracranial pressure in a supine adult. Which range is correct?
questions.e: Normal ICP in a supine adult is about 5-15 mmHg. Sustained pressures above about 20-22 mmHg are treated, because they reduce cerebral perfusion and risk herniation.

questions.s: A ventilated patient with a sudden rise in intracranial pressure and signs of impending herniation is briefly hyperventilated while mannitol is prepared. By what mechanism does hyperventilation lower ICP?
o: Increased CSF absorption by arachnoid villi
Osmotic shift of water out of the brain
Reduced CSF production by the choroid plexus
Cerebral vasoconstriction from a lower PaCO2
questions.e: Lowering PaCO2 constricts cerebral arterioles, reducing cerebral blood volume and therefore ICP within minutes. The effect is short-lived and excessive hyperventilation causes ischaemia, so it is used only briefly as a bridge.

questions.s: A 72-year-old man has had a broad-based, shuffling, magnetic gait for a year, followed by urinary urgency and incontinence and, more recently, forgetfulness. CT shows enlarged ventricles out of proportion to sulcal widening. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Gait disturbance, urinary incontinence and cognitive decline with ventriculomegaly is the triad of normal pressure hydrocephalus, which may improve after a ventriculoperitoneal shunt. In Alzheimer's disease the ventricles enlarge in proportion to cortical atrophy, and gait problems come late.

questions.s: A medical student is shown a CT scan of an extradural haematoma. Where is the blood located in this type of haemorrhage?
questions.e: An extradural haematoma lies between the inner table of the skull and the dura, usually from arterial bleeding after a fracture. A subdural haematoma lies between the dura and arachnoid, usually from torn bridging veins.

questions.s: An 80-year-old man has had progressive drowsiness for 4 weeks after a minor fall. On non-contrast CT, how does an uncomplicated subdural haematoma of this age most often appear compared with brain tissue?
questions.e: Fresh blood is hyperdense, but as a subdural clot breaks down over about three weeks it becomes isodense and then hypodense, so chronic subdural haematomas usually look darker than brain. An isodense subacute collection can be missed, so look for midline shift and effaced sulci.

questions.s: In a remote district hospital without a neurosurgeon, and with transfer impossible, a doctor is advised by phone to make an emergency burr hole in a deteriorating patient with a suspected extradural haematoma and no CT. The right pupil is fixed and dilated, and there is left hemiparesis. Where should the first burr hole be made?
questions.e: Without imaging, the first burr hole is placed in the temporal region on the side of the dilated pupil, because the third nerve is compressed by the ipsilateral haematoma; the hemiparesis is contralateral. This is a last resort when no neurosurgical help or transfer is possible.

questions.s: A 5-year-old girl has a 1.5 cm tender, mobile lymph node in the upper deep cervical chain for a week following a sore throat. She is well and has no other lumps. What is the most likely cause?
questions.e: Small, tender, mobile nodes after an upper respiratory infection in a child are almost always reactive and settle over a few weeks. Persistent, enlarging, hard or matted nodes, or systemic symptoms, would prompt investigation for tuberculosis or lymphoma.

questions.s: A 19-year-old man has a painless, rounded, doughy swelling in the midline under the chin, above the hyoid, present for years. It does not move on swallowing or tongue protrusion. Excision shows a cyst lined by keratinised squamous epithelium containing cheesy material, without skin appendages in its wall. What is the diagnosis?
questions.e: A midline submental cyst that does not move with tongue protrusion and contains keratin is a sublingual epidermoid or dermoid cyst arising from trapped ectoderm. A thyroglossal cyst moves upwards on tongue protrusion because it is attached to the tract at the hyoid.

questions.s: A 55-year-old woman with long-standing dry eyes and dry mouth and anti-Ro antibodies has had bilateral parotid swelling for years. Recently one parotid has become larger and firmer, and she has lost weight. Which complication is most likely?
questions.e: Sjögren's syndrome carries a markedly increased risk of non-Hodgkin lymphoma, typically MALT lymphoma of the parotid, and persistent enlargement of one gland with weight loss is a warning sign needing biopsy. An abscess would be painful and acutely inflamed.

questions.s: A doctor examining a patient with suspected parotitis looks inside the mouth for pus coming from the parotid duct opening. Where does the parotid (Stensen's) duct open?
o: At the tip of the sublingual papilla
questions.e: The parotid duct crosses masseter, pierces buccinator and opens on the buccal mucosa opposite the upper second molar tooth. The submandibular duct opens on the sublingual papilla beside the lingual frenulum.

questions.s: A 58-year-old man with poorly controlled diabetes who uses an inhaled corticosteroid for COPD has a sore mouth. There are creamy white plaques on the palate and buccal mucosa that wipe off with gauze, leaving a red, raw surface. What is the most appropriate treatment?
questions.e: White plaques that wipe off to leave a red base are pseudomembranous candidiasis, encouraged here by diabetes and inhaled steroids, and treated with a topical antifungal plus rinsing after inhaler use. Biopsy is for white patches that cannot be wiped off, such as leukoplakia.

questions.s: A dental surgeon in Karachi teaching an oral cancer screening session asks which part of the tongue should be examined most carefully, because it is the commonest site of carcinoma of the oral tongue. Which site is it?
questions.e: Squamous cell carcinoma of the oral tongue most often arises on the lateral border of the middle third, so the tongue should be pulled out and turned to each side during examination. The dorsum is an uncommon site.

questions.s: Waqas, 25, has a reducible swelling in the right groin that descends into the scrotum on standing. After reduction, firm pressure just above the midpoint of the inguinal ligament stops the swelling reappearing when he coughs. What type of hernia is this?
o: Spigelian hernia through the linea semilunaris
questions.e: An indirect inguinal hernia passes through the deep ring, which lies just above the midpoint of the inguinal ligament, so pressure there controls it, and it often descends into the scrotum in young men. A direct hernia pushes through the posterior wall medial to the deep ring and is not controlled by this pressure.

questions.s: During an open repair of a direct inguinal hernia, the surgeon identifies the inferior epigastric vessels. Where does the neck of a direct hernia sac lie in relation to these vessels?
o: Lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels
Within the deep inguinal ring with the cord
Medial to the inferior epigastric vessels
questions.e: A direct hernia emerges through Hesselbach's triangle, bounded by the inferior epigastric vessels laterally, the rectus sheath medially and the inguinal ligament below, so its neck lies medial to the vessels. An indirect hernia enters the deep ring lateral to them, and a femoral hernia lies below the ligament.

questions.s: A 55-year-old woman has a soft, reducible, non-tender lump in the right groin that appears on standing. It lies below and lateral to the pubic tubercle. She has no bowel symptoms. What is the most appropriate management?
o: Reassurance with review if it becomes painful
A truss and review in 6 months
questions.e: A lump below and lateral to the pubic tubercle is a femoral hernia, which has a narrow, rigid neck and a high risk of strangulation, so even an asymptomatic one should be repaired promptly. Watchful waiting is reasonable only for some minimally symptomatic inguinal hernias, and trusses do not control femoral hernias.

questions.s: A 68-year-old man has a known left inguinal hernia that became painful and irreducible 10 hours ago. He has vomited several times and his abdomen is distended. The swelling is tense and tender with red overlying skin. Pulse is 112/min. What is the most appropriate management?
o: Manual reduction under sedation, then elective mesh repair in 6 weeks
Intravenous fluids, nasogastric decompression and emergency surgery
Abdominal CT and review the next day
Analgesia and ice packs to reduce swelling
questions.e: Tenderness, red skin, tachycardia and obstruction suggest a strangulated hernia, which needs resuscitation followed by emergency exploration and repair, with resection of non-viable bowel. Forceful reduction of a strangulated hernia can return dead bowel into the abdomen and must be avoided.

questions.s: A 2-month-old boy born at 34 weeks has an intermittent swelling in the left groin that appears when he cries and reduces easily. What is the most appropriate management?
o: Herniotomy at the age of 5 years if still present
A truss until the child is walking
Mesh repair at the age of 2 years
Herniotomy on the next elective list
questions.e: Inguinal hernias in infants, especially preterm ones, have a high risk of incarceration, so herniotomy (ligation of the patent processus vaginalis) is done soon after diagnosis. Mesh repair is not used in children, and waiting years exposes the child to incarceration and testicular damage.

questions.s: A mother in Faisalabad brings her 18-month-old son with a soft swelling at the umbilicus that bulges when he cries. It reduces easily and the defect is about 1 cm. He is well. What is the most appropriate advice?
o: Strap a coin over the umbilicus
Repair with mesh at the age of 2 years
questions.e: Congenital umbilical hernias are common and most close by themselves by 4–5 years; strangulation is rare. Coin strapping does not help and can irritate the skin, and repair is planned if the hernia persists after about 4–5 years or is very large.

questions.s: Six months after an emergency laparotomy, a 50-year-old man has a bulge in his midline scar. Which factor at the time of his surgery most increased his risk of this complication?
o: Use of a non-absorbable skin stapler
Use of a midline rather than paramedian incision only
questions.e: Wound infection is the most important single risk factor for incisional hernia, along with obesity, poor closure technique, steroids and malnutrition. Skin closure does not affect the strength of the fascial layer, and early mobilisation is not a risk factor.

questions.s: An 80-year-old woman has a tender lump below the inguinal ligament. She has had no vomiting and is passing flatus. At surgery, only part of the circumference of the small bowel wall is trapped in the hernia and is dusky. What is this called?
questions.e: In a Richter hernia only part of the antimesenteric bowel wall is trapped, so it can strangulate without causing complete obstruction, delaying diagnosis. A Littre hernia contains a Meckel diverticulum, and a Maydl hernia contains two loops with the intervening loop strangulated inside the abdomen.

questions.s: During repair of a femoral hernia, the surgeon must take care not to damage a structure immediately lateral to the femoral canal. Which structure is it?
questions.e: The femoral canal lies within the femoral sheath, with the femoral vein immediately lateral to it, so sutures placed laterally can narrow or injure the vein. The lacunar ligament forms the medial boundary, and the femoral nerve lies outside the sheath lateral to the artery.

questions.s: A 40-year-old man has an uncomplicated primary right inguinal hernia that troubles him at work. He is fit for surgery. Which elective open repair is the standard choice?
o: Bassini repair with tension on the suture line
questions.e: The Lichtenstein tension-free mesh repair is the standard open repair for adult inguinal hernias, with low recurrence and quick recovery. Herniotomy alone is used in children, whose problem is only a patent processus vaginalis, and tension repairs have higher recurrence.

questions.s: A 45-year-old man has a painless 5 cm swelling on his back for years. It is soft, lobulated, mobile and not attached to the skin, and its edge slips under the examining finger. It does not transilluminate. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: A soft, lobulated, mobile, slow-growing swelling with a slipping edge and free skin is a lipoma, the commonest benign soft tissue tumour. Sebaceous (epidermoid) cysts are attached to the skin and often have a punctum, and liposarcoma is suspected when a lump is large, deep, hard or growing quickly.

questions.s: A 30-year-old woman has a 2 cm smooth, firm, round swelling on the back of her neck. It is attached to the skin, with a small dark central punctum, and moves with the skin over deeper tissues. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: An epidermoid (sebaceous) cyst arises within the skin, so it is tethered to it and often shows a central punctum. A lipoma lies in subcutaneous fat with free skin and no punctum, and a lymph node is deep to the skin.

questions.s: A 24-year-old woman has a firm, smooth, 1.5 cm swelling on the back of her wrist that becomes more prominent when she flexes the wrist. It transilluminates and is not tender. What is the most likely diagnosis?
o: Giant cell tumour of tendon sheath
questions.e: A ganglion is a mucoid cyst arising from a joint capsule or tendon sheath, most often on the dorsum of the wrist; it is firm, smooth and transilluminates. Many resolve spontaneously, so reassurance or aspiration is often enough, and excision can be offered for troublesome symptoms.

questions.s: A 4-year-old girl has a painless 1 cm round swelling at the outer end of her left eyebrow, present since infancy. It is smooth, firm and fixed to deeper tissue but not to the skin. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Congenital dermoid cysts occur along lines of embryonic fusion, classically at the outer end of the eyebrow, and are deep to the skin and often attached to periosteum. Haemangiomas are compressible, usually red or bluish, and many enlarge in infancy then regress.

questions.s: A 66-year-old woman has a shallow, painful ulcer above the medial malleolus with surrounding brown pigmentation and hard, tight skin. She has varicose veins. Her foot pulses are hard to feel because of oedema. What must be done before applying compression bandaging?
o: Take a biopsy from the ulcer edge
Arrange venous duplex for varicose vein surgery
questions.e: Compression is the main treatment for venous ulcers, but it can cause ischaemic damage if arterial disease is present, so the ankle–brachial pressure index must be measured first (compression is usually safe if it is above about 0.8). Biopsy is only needed for atypical or non-healing ulcers.

questions.s: A 70-year-old smoker has a painful, punched-out ulcer on the tip of his big toe. The surrounding skin is pale, shiny and hairless, and the foot pulses are absent. The pain is worse when he lies flat at night. What is the most likely type of ulcer?
questions.e: Painful, punched-out ulcers on the toes with absent pulses, hairless shiny skin and rest pain relieved by hanging the leg down indicate arterial insufficiency. Neuropathic ulcers are painless, occur over pressure points such as the metatarsal heads, and often have palpable pulses.

questions.s: A 55-year-old man with long-standing diabetes has a painless deep ulcer under the head of his first metatarsal surrounded by thick callus. The foot is warm, pulses are palpable, and he cannot feel a 10 g monofilament on the sole. What is the main cause of this ulcer?
o: Chronic venous hypertension of the leg
questions.e: Loss of protective sensation means repeated pressure under the metatarsal head goes unnoticed, producing a painless callus-rimmed ulcer on a warm foot with good pulses. Arterial ulcers occur on a cold, pulseless foot and are painful.

questions.s: Ayesha, 28, has a 7 mm firm, brownish nodule on her shin that appeared some months after an insect bite. It is attached to the skin but moves freely over the deeper tissues, and when the skin on either side is pinched together the lesion dimples inwards. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: A dermatofibroma is a benign fibrous skin nodule, common on the legs of young women and often following minor trauma such as a bite; dimpling on lateral pinching is characteristic. A neurofibroma is soft and can be pushed into the skin (buttonhole sign), and an epidermoid cyst is a smooth dome, often with a central punctum.

questions.s: A 58-year-old woman has an intermittent painful lump in the lower abdomen. On standing and straining, a small tender swelling can be felt at the lateral edge of the right rectus muscle, below the umbilicus at about the level of the arcuate line. It is difficult to define because it seems to lie beneath the external oblique aponeurosis. She has never had abdominal surgery. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: A Spigelian hernia passes through the linea semilunaris at the lateral edge of rectus, usually near the arcuate line, and often stays deep to an intact external oblique aponeurosis, so it is easily missed; its narrow neck carries a real risk of strangulation. A rectus sheath haematoma lies within the rectus, usually follows coughing or anticoagulation and does not come and go with straining, and an incisional hernia needs a previous scar.

questions.s: A 70-year-old farmer from Sargodha has a slowly growing nodule on the side of his nose for 2 years. It is pearly with a rolled edge, fine telangiectasia over it and a small central crust. There are no palpable lymph nodes. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: A slow-growing pearly nodule with a rolled edge and telangiectasia on sun-exposed skin of the face is a basal cell carcinoma. Keratoacanthoma grows rapidly over weeks with a central keratin plug, and seborrhoeic keratoses look waxy and 'stuck on'.

questions.s: A 65-year-old man is told he has a basal cell carcinoma on his cheek. He asks whether it is likely to spread to other parts of his body. Which statement best describes its behaviour?
o: It usually spreads early to regional lymph nodes
It invades locally but very rarely metastasises
It spreads mainly by the bloodstream to the lungs
questions.e: Basal cell carcinoma grows slowly and can destroy local tissues, including cartilage and bone (hence 'rodent ulcer'), but metastasis is extremely rare. Squamous cell carcinoma is the skin cancer that more often spreads to regional lymph nodes.

questions.s: A 50-year-old man had extensive burns to his leg 30 years ago. An area in the old scar broke down 6 months ago into an ulcer that keeps enlarging and now has raised, everted edges and bleeds easily. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: A Marjolin ulcer is an aggressive squamous cell carcinoma arising in chronic scars or ulcers, especially old burn scars; an enlarging ulcer with everted edges must be biopsied. Venous ulcers have sloping edges and occur in the gaiter area with signs of venous disease.

questions.s: A 40-year-old woman has a melanoma excised from her calf. Which feature of the histology report is the most important prognostic factor in localised disease?
o: The number of mitoses per field only
questions.e: Breslow thickness, measured in millimetres from the granular layer to the deepest tumour cell, is the strongest predictor of outcome in localised melanoma and guides excision margins and sentinel node biopsy. Ulceration and mitotic rate add information, but diameter and colour do not predict prognosis.

questions.s: A 45-year-old man has a 9 mm mole on his back that has enlarged over 6 months, with an irregular border and several shades of brown and black. What is the most appropriate first step?
o: Excision biopsy with a 2 mm margin
Shave biopsy of the raised part
Wide local excision with a 2 cm margin
questions.e: A lesion suspicious for melanoma is removed whole with a narrow (about 2 mm) margin so that the pathologist can measure Breslow thickness; the definitive wider margin is based on that thickness. Shave biopsy may cut through the tumour and prevent accurate staging.

questions.s: A 62-year-old man has a dark brown streak under the nail of his right big toe that has widened over a year. The pigment now extends onto the skin of the nail fold. He recalls no injury. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Spread of pigment from the nail onto the surrounding nail fold (Hutchinson sign) with a widening streak suggests subungual (acral lentiginous) melanoma, the commonest melanoma type in people with darker skin. A haematoma grows out with the nail and does not involve the nail fold.

questions.s: A 68-year-old retired traffic policeman has several rough, scaly, pink patches on his bald scalp and the backs of his hands. They feel like sandpaper. Which malignancy can these lesions progress to?
questions.e: Rough, scaly patches on chronically sun-exposed skin are actinic keratoses, which are premalignant and can progress to squamous cell carcinoma. A lesion that becomes thick, tender or ulcerated should be biopsied; actinic keratoses are not precursors of basal cell carcinoma.

questions.s: A 9-year-old boy, the child of a consanguineous marriage, has extreme sun sensitivity, heavy freckling of exposed skin and has already had two basal cell carcinomas removed. Which cellular defect underlies his condition?
questions.e: Xeroderma pigmentosum is an autosomal recessive defect of nucleotide excision repair, so UV-induced thymine dimers are not removed, leading to skin cancers in childhood. Mismatch repair defects cause Lynch syndrome with colorectal and endometrial cancer.

questions.s: A 22-year-old farm labourer from rural Sindh has had fever and a painful, swollen right thigh for 10 days. The thigh is woody hard and tender, but there is no fluctuation or skin redness. There is no history of injury. What is the most appropriate investigation to confirm the diagnosis?
o: Venous duplex scan of the leg
questions.e: Fever with a woody, tender muscle swelling in a young person in a tropical region suggests pyomyositis, a Staphylococcus aureus abscess within skeletal muscle; ultrasound (or MRI) shows the intramuscular collection and guides drainage. Plain X-ray and a raised CK do not show the abscess.

questions.s: A 58-year-old man with poorly controlled diabetes has had scrotal pain and fever for 2 days. The scrotal skin is swollen, purplish with black patches, crepitus is felt in the perineum, and there is a foul smell. BP is 90/60 mmHg. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Fournier gangrene is necrotising fasciitis of the perineum and genitalia, typically in diabetic men, with rapidly spreading pain, skin necrosis, crepitus and sepsis; it needs resuscitation, broad-spectrum antibiotics and urgent radical debridement. Epididymo-orchitis does not cause skin necrosis or crepitus.

questions.s: A 35-year-old woman has a spreading, warm, tender red area on her lower leg after a small cut. She is afebrile and there is no pus or fluctuation. She has no penicillin allergy. Which oral antibiotic is the most appropriate first-line treatment?
questions.e: Non-purulent cellulitis is usually caused by Streptococcus pyogenes or Staphylococcus aureus, and flucloxacillin covers both. Metronidazole covers anaerobes only, and ciprofloxacin has poor streptococcal activity.

questions.s: A 22-year-old hairy, overweight man who drives a rickshaw has recurrent painful swelling and discharge at the top of his natal cleft. There are several small midline pits in the cleft. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Pilonidal disease occurs in the natal cleft of young hairy men, especially those who sit for long periods, as hairs drive into the skin and form midline pits and sinuses that become infected. A fistula-in-ano opens near the anus and connects with the anal canal.

questions.s: A 30-year-old tailor pricked her index fingertip with a needle 4 days ago. The pulp of the finger is now tense, red and extremely painful with throbbing that keeps her awake. The nail fold is normal. What is the most appropriate management?
o: Oral antibiotics alone and review in a week
Incision and drainage of the pulp space
questions.e: A felon is an abscess of the fingertip pulp, a closed compartment divided by fibrous septa, so pus under pressure can cause necrosis or osteomyelitis of the distal phalanx; it needs incision and drainage with antibiotics. Nail removal treats some paronychia, which affects the nail fold.

questions.s: A 28-year-old obese woman who smokes has had recurrent painful nodules and abscesses in both armpits and groins for 3 years, healing with rope-like scars and sinus tracts. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Hidradenitis suppurativa is a chronic inflammatory disease of hair follicles in flexural sites, giving recurrent painful nodules, abscesses, sinus tracts and scarring; obesity and smoking are risk factors. Simple furuncles do not form interconnected sinus tracts in a typical flexural distribution.

questions.s: A 60-year-old man has a large, painful swelling on the back of his neck with several pus-discharging openings over it and fever. He has never been told of any illness. Before or with drainage of this lesion, which test is most important?
questions.e: A carbuncle (a group of infected hair follicles discharging through several openings, usually Staphylococcus aureus) on the nape of the neck is strongly associated with diabetes, which should always be checked. Undiagnosed diabetes worsens infection and healing and needs treatment alongside drainage.

questions.s: Zainab's first baby, a 5-week-old boy, has had worsening forceful vomiting after every feed for a week. The vomit is milky without bile, and he is hungry immediately after. During a test feed a firm, olive-sized mass is felt in the right upper abdomen. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Projectile non-bilious vomiting in a hungry 2–8-week-old, commoner in firstborn boys, with a palpable olive-shaped mass is typical of hypertrophic pyloric stenosis. Malrotation with volvulus and duodenal atresia cause bilious vomiting, and duodenal atresia presents in the first day or two of life.

questions.s: A 6-week-old boy has projectile non-bilious vomiting, but no mass can be felt during a test feed. Which investigation is most appropriate to confirm hypertrophic pyloric stenosis?
questions.e: Ultrasound shows a thickened, elongated pyloric muscle, is quick and uses no radiation, so it is the investigation of choice when the mass cannot be felt. A contrast meal also shows the narrowed canal but exposes the infant to radiation and aspiration risk.

questions.s: A 4-week-old boy with pyloric stenosis has been vomiting for 10 days. Which blood gas and electrolyte pattern is most expected?
questions.e: Repeated vomiting of gastric contents loses hydrochloric acid, causing hypochloraemic metabolic alkalosis, and renal compensation for dehydration increases potassium loss. Acidosis develops only very late with severe dehydration and shock.

questions.s: An ultrasound confirms pyloric stenosis in a 5-week-old boy. He is moderately dehydrated, with Na 132 mmol/L, K 3.0 mmol/L, Cl 84 mmol/L and bicarbonate 34 mmol/L. What is the most appropriate next step?
o: Pyloromyotomy on the emergency list tonight after one fluid bolus
Endoscopic balloon dilatation of the pylorus
IV saline, dextrose and potassium, then surgery
questions.e: Pyloric stenosis is a medical, not surgical, emergency: dehydration and alkalosis are corrected with intravenous saline, dextrose and potassium before pyloromyotomy, because anaesthesia with uncorrected alkalosis risks postoperative apnoea. Surgery is done once chloride and bicarbonate are normal.

questions.s: A dehydrated infant with pyloric stenosis has a high serum bicarbonate, but his urine is acidic. What is the main reason for this paradoxical aciduria?
o: Distal sodium reabsorption in exchange for hydrogen ions
Ketone bodies from starvation are excreted in the urine
Bicarbonate is reabsorbed in excess in the loop of Henle
Lactic acid from poor perfusion is filtered into the urine
questions.e: With volume depletion, aldosterone drives distal sodium reabsorption, and when chloride and potassium are depleted the kidney exchanges sodium for hydrogen ions, producing acidic urine despite systemic alkalosis. Correcting volume, chloride and potassium stops this.

questions.s: Ahmed, a 9-month-old boy, has episodes of inconsolable crying every 15–20 minutes, during which he draws up his legs and goes pale. Between episodes he is lethargic. He has vomited twice and passed a stool of blood mixed with mucus. A sausage-shaped mass is felt in the right upper abdomen. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Intermittent colicky pain with pallor and drawing up of the legs, lethargy, 'redcurrant jelly' stool and a sausage-shaped mass in an infant indicate intussusception. Meckel diverticulum usually causes painless rectal bleeding, and infant colic does not cause bloody stools or a mass.

questions.s: A 1-year-old girl has colicky abdominal pain and vomiting. Intussusception is suspected, but no mass can be felt. Which investigation is most appropriate?
questions.e: Ultrasound is highly sensitive and specific for intussusception, showing a 'target' or 'doughnut' sign in cross-section, and uses no radiation. A plain X-ray may be normal or show non-specific signs, and CT is unnecessary in most children.

questions.s: An 8-month-old boy has ileocolic intussusception confirmed on ultrasound. After fluid resuscitation he is haemodynamically stable with a soft abdomen and no signs of peritonitis. What is the most appropriate treatment?
o: Emergency laparotomy and manual reduction of the bowel
Nasogastric tube and observation for 24 hours
questions.e: In a stable child without peritonitis or perforation, image-guided air or hydrostatic enema reduction is first-line and succeeds in most cases. Surgery is needed if enema reduction fails, or if there is peritonitis, perforation or shock that does not respond to resuscitation.

questions.s: A 10-month-old girl has had intussusception symptoms for 3 days. She has a temperature of 38.8 °C, a rigid, tender abdomen and remains tachycardic after fluid boluses. X-ray shows free air under the diaphragm. What is the most appropriate management?
questions.e: Peritonitis and pneumoperitoneum indicate perforation, which is an absolute contraindication to enema reduction, so the child needs resuscitation and laparotomy with resection of non-viable bowel. Enema in this setting can worsen contamination of the peritoneal cavity.

questions.s: A 6-year-old boy has his second episode of intussusception in 3 months. Most intussusceptions in infants have no identifiable lead point. In a child of his age with recurrent episodes, which lead point is most likely?
questions.e: Intussusception in older children, or recurrent episodes, is more often due to a pathological lead point, of which Meckel diverticulum is the commonest; polyps, duplications and lymphoma are others. In infants the usual cause is lymphoid hyperplasia of Peyer patches after a viral illness.

questions.s: At his 8-week check, a baby boy's right testis cannot be felt in the scrotum but is palpable in the inguinal canal and cannot be brought down. At what age should orchidopexy ideally be done if the testis remains undescended?
questions.e: Testes that have not descended by about 6 months rarely descend later, and orchidopexy between 6 and 18 months helps preserve fertility and allows the testis to be examined for later cancer. Delaying surgery leads to progressive damage of germ cells.

questions.s: Parents ask about the long-term risks for their son with an undescended testis, who is due for orchidopexy. Which risk does this condition increase?
questions.e: Cryptorchidism increases the risk of testicular germ cell tumours (especially seminoma) and of subfertility; early orchidopexy improves fertility and allows self-examination, though it does not remove the cancer risk entirely. The contralateral descended testis also has a slightly increased risk.

questions.s: A 4-year-old boy's left testis is sometimes not seen in the scrotum. On examination it lies at the top of the scrotum but can be brought fully into the scrotum, where it stays after release until he is tickled. What is the most appropriate management?
questions.e: A retractile testis can be brought down and stays in the scrotum after release, retreating only because of an active cremasteric reflex; it needs reassurance with follow-up because a few later ascend. Orchidopexy is for testes that cannot be brought into the scrotum or that will not stay there.

questions.s: A 1-year-old boy has an empty left hemiscrotum. The testis cannot be felt in the groin even under general anaesthesia. The right testis is normal. What is the most appropriate next step?
o: CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis
questions.e: For a unilateral impalpable testis, laparoscopy is both diagnostic and therapeutic: it finds an intra-abdominal testis for staged orchidopexy or confirms a vanished testis. Imaging such as ultrasound or CT cannot reliably exclude an intra-abdominal testis and exposes the child to radiation with CT.

questions.s: A term newborn has not passed meconium by 48 hours and has a distended abdomen and bilious vomiting. Rectal examination is followed by an explosive gush of stool and gas. Which investigation confirms the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Delayed meconium, distension and an explosive stool after rectal examination suggest Hirschsprung disease, confirmed by a rectal suction biopsy showing absent ganglion cells with increased acetylcholinesterase-positive nerve fibres. A contrast enema can show a transition zone but does not confirm the diagnosis.

questions.s: A 6-day-old baby who had been feeding well suddenly develops green vomiting. The abdomen is not distended and the baby looks well. What is the most appropriate urgent investigation?
questions.e: Bilious vomiting in a neonate is malrotation with midgut volvulus until proven otherwise, and an urgent upper GI contrast study shows the abnormal position of the duodenojejunal flexure; delay can lead to loss of the whole midgut. A non-distended abdomen does not exclude volvulus, which obstructs high in the gut.

questions.s: A thin 78-year-old woman has colicky abdominal pain and vomiting for 2 days. She also has pain along the inner side of her right thigh down to the knee, which worsens when the hip is extended and internally rotated. No groin lump is visible. CT shows a loop of small bowel trapped next to the pubic ramus. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Obturator hernias occur in thin elderly women; compression of the obturator nerve causes pain down the medial thigh (Howship–Romberg sign), and there is usually no visible lump, so they present with small bowel obstruction. A femoral hernia is usually palpable below and lateral to the pubic tubercle.

questions.s: During repair of a large left inguinal hernia in a 65-year-old man, the surgeon finds that part of the wall of the hernia sac is formed by the sigmoid colon. What is this called?
questions.e: In a sliding hernia a retroperitoneal organ (sigmoid colon on the left, caecum on the right, or bladder) forms part of the sac wall, so the surgeon must avoid opening that part of the sac. A pantaloon hernia has both direct and indirect components straddling the inferior epigastric vessels.

questions.s: After an open inguinal hernia repair, a 35-year-old man has numbness over the root of his penis, the front of his scrotum and the upper medial thigh. Which nerve was most likely injured?
o: Lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh
questions.e: The ilioinguinal nerve runs through the inguinal canal on the spermatic cord and supplies the skin of the upper medial thigh, the root of the penis and the anterior scrotum, so it is at risk during open repair. The femoral branch of the genitofemoral nerve supplies a small area of skin over the femoral triangle.

questions.s: A 40-year-old labourer has a small, tender lump in the midline halfway between his umbilicus and xiphisternum. It appears on straining, and a small defect is felt in the linea alba. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: An epigastric hernia is a protrusion of extraperitoneal fat through a small defect in the linea alba above the umbilicus, and it is often tender for its size. Divarication of the recti causes a long midline bulge on straining without a discrete defect or tenderness.

questions.s: A 32-year-old man has a sebaceous cyst on his upper back that became red, hot, painful and fluctuant 3 days ago. What is the most appropriate management?
o: Complete excision of the cyst with its wall today
Incision and drainage now; excise the cyst later
questions.e: An infected, fluctuant epidermoid cyst is incised and drained first, because the inflamed wall is hard to excise completely and recurrence is common; excision of the cyst wall is done later once settled. Antibiotics alone do not drain an established abscess.

questions.s: An 18-year-old has eight light-brown flat skin patches larger than 15 mm, freckles in both armpits and several soft, painless nodules on the trunk that can be pushed into the skin. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Multiple café-au-lait macules, axillary freckling and cutaneous neurofibromas meet diagnostic criteria for neurofibromatosis type 1. Neurofibromatosis type 2 presents mainly with bilateral vestibular schwannomas and few skin signs.

questions.s: A 23-year-old woman has a chronic ulcer on the side of her neck over a matted cervical lymph node mass. The edges of the ulcer are thin, bluish and undermined. What is the most likely cause?
questions.e: Undermined, bluish edges are typical of a tuberculous ulcer, here from a caseating cervical node that has broken through the skin (scrofuloderma). A basal cell carcinoma has a rolled edge, a squamous cell carcinoma an everted edge, and a gumma a punched-out edge.

questions.s: A 75-year-old bedbound man on a medical ward is at high risk of pressure ulcers. Which measure is the most important in preventing them?
o: Applying talcum powder to the skin
questions.e: Pressure ulcers result from sustained pressure causing tissue ischaemia, so regular repositioning, together with pressure-relieving mattresses, is the main preventive measure. Massaging bony prominences can damage tissue further, and antibiotics do not prevent pressure damage.

questions.s: A 65-year-old farmer who smokes a hookah has a painless ulcer on his lower lip for 4 months. It has raised, everted, indurated edges and bleeds on touch. A firm node is felt under the chin. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Squamous cell carcinoma of the lower lip is linked to sun exposure and tobacco and forms an indurated ulcer with everted edges, spreading to submental and submandibular nodes. Basal cell carcinoma rarely involves the vermilion of the lower lip and seldom spreads to nodes.

questions.s: A 35-year-old woman has had a melanoma 1.6 mm thick removed from her forearm. There are no palpable axillary nodes and staging CT is clear. At wide local excision, which procedure is offered to stage the regional nodes?
o: Fine-needle aspiration of an impalpable node
questions.e: Sentinel lymph node biopsy identifies the first draining node using a tracer and is offered for melanomas of intermediate thickness without clinical nodal disease, giving important staging and prognostic information. Elective full node dissection adds morbidity without proven survival benefit.

questions.s: A 60-year-old man has a dome-shaped nodule on his cheek that grew to 1.5 cm in just 6 weeks. It has a central crater filled with keratin. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Keratoacanthoma grows rapidly over weeks into a dome-shaped nodule with a central keratin plug, and may regress, but it is hard to distinguish from squamous cell carcinoma and is usually excised. Basal cell carcinoma grows slowly over months to years.

questions.s: A 55-year-old woman has a fever and a bright red, raised, shiny plaque on her cheek with a sharply demarcated edge that she can feel with her finger. Which organism is the most likely cause?
questions.e: Erysipelas is a superficial form of cellulitis involving the dermis and dermal lymphatics, giving a raised, sharply demarcated red plaque, and is usually caused by Streptococcus pyogenes. Herpes zoster causes a painful dermatomal vesicular rash rather than a raised erythematous plaque.

questions.s: A 26-year-old woman has a painful, red, swollen fold of skin at the side of her fingernail 2 days after trimming her cuticles. A small yellow collection of pus is visible under the skin fold. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Acute paronychia is a bacterial infection of the nail fold, usually Staphylococcus aureus after minor trauma, and a visible pus collection needs drainage by lifting the fold. A felon involves the pulp of the fingertip, and herpetic whitlow forms grouped vesicles rather than pus.

questions.s: A 19-year-old student has had his third episode of an infected ingrowing toenail on the side of his big toe. Each settled with antibiotics. What is the most appropriate definitive treatment?
o: Removal of the whole nail without treating the nail bed
Wedge excision of the nail edge with phenolisation of the nail bed
questions.e: For recurrent ingrowing toenails, wedge excision of the affected nail edge with chemical ablation of that part of the nail matrix using phenol prevents regrowth of the offending edge. Simple nail avulsion has a high recurrence rate, and antibiotics treat only the infection.

questions.s: A 6-week-old boy undergoes Ramstedt pyloromyotomy for pyloric stenosis. Which layers are divided in this operation?
o: The pyloric muscle down to the intact mucosa
The full thickness of the pyloric wall, then closed transversely
The mucosa only, through an endoscope
questions.e: In Ramstedt pyloromyotomy the hypertrophied pyloric muscle is split longitudinally down to the submucosa, so that the mucosa bulges through while remaining intact; a mucosal breach must be recognised and repaired. A full-thickness incision closed transversely describes a pyloroplasty, which is not used for infants.

questions.s: A 3-week-old baby was given an oral antibiotic for pertussis contact 10 days ago and now has projectile non-bilious vomiting. Ultrasound shows pyloric stenosis. Which antibiotic is known to increase this risk in early infancy?
questions.e: Erythromycin given in the first weeks of life is associated with an increased risk of infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis, probably through its motilin-agonist effect on the pylorus. Amoxicillin and cephalosporins are not linked to this condition.

questions.s: In infants with intussusception, which segment of bowel most commonly telescopes into which?
questions.e: Ileocolic intussusception, in which the terminal ileum enters the caecum and colon, accounts for most cases in infants, often with lymphoid hyperplasia of Peyer patches as the starting point. Small bowel (ileo-ileal) intussusceptions are less common and often transient.

questions.s: A mother brings her 9-month-old son with a soft swelling at the umbilicus that gets bigger when he cries. It reduces easily, the fascial defect is about 1 cm wide, and the baby is feeding well and thriving. What is the most appropriate management?
o: Elective repair at the next available list
Strapping a coin over the umbilicus
Urgent ultrasound of the abdominal wall
questions.e: Umbilical hernias in infants are common, rarely strangulate and most close spontaneously as the umbilical ring contracts, so the parents are reassured and repair is considered only if the hernia persists into the early school years or is very large. Strapping or coins do not speed closure and can irritate the skin.

questions.s: A 1-year-old boy has an empty right hemiscrotum. The testis is felt in the groin, lying above and lateral to the external ring, superficial to the external oblique aponeurosis, outside the normal line of descent. What is the most common site for this type of testis?
questions.e: An ectopic testis has left the normal path of descent, and the commonest site is the superficial inguinal pouch, superficial to the external oblique aponeurosis. Perineal, femoral and penile sites are much rarer; ectopic testes do not descend spontaneously and need orchidopexy.

questions.s: A newborn boy has a urethral opening on the underside of the penis just below the glans, with a hooded foreskin and mild downward curvature. His parents ask for circumcision for religious reasons. What is the most appropriate advice?
o: Circumcise now and repair the urethra at a later date
No treatment is needed, as the condition resolves
questions.e: In hypospadias the foreskin is often used as tissue for the repair, so circumcision is deferred until reconstruction, usually done in infancy; the parents' wish can be respected at the time of repair. Hypospadias does not resolve by itself, and dilatation has no role.
